question: Pipe P can fill (7)/(9) part of a tank in 14 hours and pipe Q can fill (5)/(9) part of the same tank in 20 hours. Both P and Q were kept open for 2 hours, then both were closed. Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 6 hours. Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Time for P to fill the tank = 14 × 9/7 = 18 hours.

Time for Q to fill the tank = 20 × 9/5 = 36 hours.

Work done by P and Q in 2 hours = 2 × (1/18 + 1/36) = 1/6 of the tank.

R empties 1/6 of the tank in 6 hours, so R's total time to empty the tank = 36 hours.

Combined efficiency of P, Q, and R = 1/18 + 1/36 − 1/36 = 1/18 per hour.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time for pipe P to fill 7/9 part = 14 hours.

Time for pipe Q to fill 5/9 part = 20 hours.

Time for pipe R to empty the filled part = 6 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time for P to fill the complete tank = 14 × 9/7 = 18 hours.

⇒ Time for Q to fill the complete tank = 20 × 9/5 = 36 hours.

⇒ Part of the tank filled by P in 1 hour = 1/18

⇒ Part of the tank filled by Q in 1 hour = 1/36

⇒ Part of the tank filled by P and Q in 2 hours = 2 × (1/18 + 1/36) = 2 × (3/36) = 1/6.

⇒ Pipe R empties this 1/6 filled part in 6 hours.

⇒ Time taken by R to empty the complete tank = 6 × 6 = 36 hours.

⇒ Let Total Work = LCM of (18, 36, 36) = 36 units.

⇒ Combined efficiency of P, Q, and R = 2 + 1 − 1 = 2 units/hr.

⇒ Time taken by P, Q, and R together to fill the tank = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time = 36 ÷ 2 = 18 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Concept

If a pipe fills a tank in x hours, its efficiency is positive (1/x). If a pipe empties the tank in y hours, its efficiency is taken as negative (−1/y).

Combined Work Rule

When multiple pipes are opened simultaneously, their combined efficiency is simply the algebraic sum of their individual efficiencies.

Fractional Work

If a/b part of a task is completed in D days (or hours), then the entire task will be completed in D × (b/a) days.
